prompt: Here's the OpenTelemetry Collector config we're running in production today — take a look. We instrumented the checkout service with OTel and every trace flows through this Collector to our trace store (Tempo). Someone added a sampler a while back to cut storage/egress costs, and it worked — the bill dropped — but on-call has been complaining ever since that they can't find the traces they actually need during incidents. Walk me through what's wrong with this sampling setup and how you'd optimize it so we stay inside the same volume budget without losing the traces that matter.
givenCode:
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318

processors:
  # HEAD sampling: this decision is made per-trace at ingest time, right as the
  # first span for a trace arrives at the Collector -- long before anyone knows
  # whether that trace will end up being an error or a slow outlier or just a
  # boring successful request. The processor is stateless and has zero visibility
  # into the eventual outcome of the trace.
  probabilistic_sampler:
    hash_seed: 22
    sampling_percentage: 10   # flat 10% keep-rate, applied uniformly to every trace

  batch:
    timeout: 5s
    send_batch_size: 512

exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo.observability.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [probabilistic_sampler, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/tempo]
